data.long_meaning: Originates from the Persian word 'Shejadan', which means 'Sovereign, Ruler, Powerful'. It was a common name among Persian and Arab rulers. The name Shezad carries the meaning “Sovereign, Ruler, Powerful” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Persian tradition and is also used in Persian, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Shezad usually hope their child will grow to embody sovereign, ruler, powerful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Over time, it reached various parts of the world, including India, where it was adopted by some influential Hindu families, contributing to the diversity and multiculturalism of the subcontinent.

historical_references.reference: Shezad was a title given to some Hindu rulers in the Deccan region during the Islamic Sultanate period. It is believed to have originated from Shahzada, meaning 'royal prince' in Persian.
historical_references.context: During the Islamic Sultanate period in India, the Deccan region saw the rule of several Hindu dynasties. These rulers adopted Islamic cultural practices, including the use of titles like Shezad, which were Persian in origin.

historical_references.reference: Shezad Jaipur was a Rajput king who ruled in the early 18th century. He is known for his alliance with the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb against the Marathas.
historical_references.context: Shezad Jaipur, also known as Jai Singh II, was a Rajput king of Amber (Jaipur). He allied with the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb against the Marathas in the Battle of Bhima-Bhor, which took place in 1704. Shezad's loyalty to the Mughals helped him maintain his kingdom and secure a place in Mughal history.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shezad, which originated from the Hindu community in India, has gained popularity beyond its traditional usage within the community. The name, which is believed to have Persian or Arabic roots, has been increasingly adopted by individuals from various religious backgrounds as a result of the Islamisation of Hindu names and the globalisation of Indian names. This trend is evident on social media platforms where individuals of diverse backgrounds use the name Shezad. The entertainment industry has also seen an increase in the usage of this name, with notable figures such as Shezad Dawood, a British-Pakistani filmmaker, and Shezad Latif, a Pakistani actor, bearing the name. Furthermore, educational institutions have reported an increase in the enrolment of students with the name Shezad, reflecting the growing acceptance and popularity of this name across diverse communities and geographies.
